met-when.says: The shared movement parser admits finite absolute coordinates or own compass directions with signed distances, and returns null for malformed or overflowing input without mutating the starting pose.

The shared planar movement operation advances toward its target by at most a finite nonnegative distance, preserves heading when stationary, handles overflowing intermediate distances, and refuses invalid arguments. Compass readings are invariant under complete rotations.

provenance.derivedBy: Hai Xudi, source author review; no independent review asserted

standard.applicability: Source-observed component model for bounded game geometry; complete ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 conformance unassessed

system.name: MOOSE shared geometry
system.description: MOOSE owns pure geometry; FeltOS forwards its public functions and applies world admission; Farstone calls those same movement functions for client prediction.

stakeholders.name: Farstone and other FeltOS game players

concerns.statement: The shared movement parser admits finite absolute coordinates or own compass directions with signed distances, and returns null for malformed or overflowing input without mutating the starting pose.

The shared planar movement operation advances toward its target by at most a finite nonnegative distance, preserves heading when stationary, handles overflowing intermediate distances, and refuses invalid arguments. Compass readings are invariant under complete rotations.

viewpoints.name: Functional
viewpoints.method: Trace actual Farstone movement prediction through the FeltOS geometry forwarder to MOOSE; compare against FeltOS authoritative spaceCapability and stepToward.

models.content: parseTarget retains finite target syntax, rejects inherited Object properties and checks computed coordinate finiteness; a malformed command is not a movement.

stepInPlane validates inputs, clamps interpolation to [0,1], uses scaled displacement for overflow and never writes world state. nearestCompass normalizes heading modulo 360 before angular comparison.

decisions.statement: Repair pure movement once in MOOSE while retaining FeltOS public names and the t/xy/heading result consumed by authoritative and predicted movement.
decisions.rationale: Duplicating movement rules would cause server/client drift.
